name: Pāṇini
summary: Author of the Aṣṭādhyāyī, the grammar that fixed classical Sanskrit and described the Vedic language; Patañjali calls him 'Dākṣīputra', son of Dākṣī. He names ten predecessors (Āpiśali, Kāśyapa, Gārgya, Gālava, Cākravarmaṇa, Bhāradvāja, Śākaṭāyana, Śākalya, Senaka, Sphoṭāyana).

tradition.text: a sage of old who received the phoneme list from Śiva

realization_account.text: After austerities he received the fourteen phoneme-sūtras from Maheśvara (Śiva), who sounded them on his drum; from them he proclaimed the whole of grammar (Pāṇinīya Śikṣā 56–57; Nandikeśvara-kāśikā). A later story (Kathāsaritsāgara) makes him a dull pupil of Varṣa who won Śiva's grace by tapas.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Kātyāyana
summary: Author of the vārttikas on Pāṇini. Tradition credits a Kātyāyana with the White Yajurveda Prātiśākhya, Śrautasūtra and Śulbasūtra and the Ṛgveda index, and identifies him with Vararuci; whether these are one person is doubted by scholars.

name: Patañjali (the grammarian)
summary: Author of the Vyākaraṇa-Mahābhāṣya. The tradition identifies him with Patañjali of the Yoga Sūtra (tch:patanjali); most scholars distinguish the two. Kept as a separate id so that both accounts stay visible.

tradition.text: an incarnation of the serpent Śeṣa, identical with the author of the Yoga Sūtra

scholarly.text: mid-2nd c. BCE (the Mahābhāṣya refers to sacrificing for Puṣyamitra)

realization_account.text: Tradition regards him as Śeṣa (Ananta) incarnate and as the one who purified speech by grammar, the mind by yoga and the body by medicine (a widely quoted invocatory verse).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Yāska
summary: Author of the Nirukta, the Vedāṅga of etymology; he reports the views of Nairuktas, Aitihāsikas, Yājñikas and grammarians and of many named predecessors (Śākaṭāyana, Gārgya, Aupamanyava, Aurṇavābha, Śākapūṇi, Kautsa and others).

scholarly.text: generally placed before Pāṇini (mid-1st millennium BCE); date uncertain

name: Piṅgala
summary: Author of the Chandaḥśāstra, the root text of prosody. The kinship with Pāṇini is a late report (low confidence).

tradition.text: a sage sometimes called a nāga; a late tradition makes him Pāṇini's younger brother

name: Lagadha
summary: The 'great-souled' teacher whose knowledge of time the Vedāṅga Jyotiṣa sets out (v. 2); known only from that text.

name: Śaunaka
summary: Ṛgvedic teacher to whom tradition ascribes the Ṛgveda Prātiśākhya, the Bṛhaddevatā, the Ṛgvidhāna and several indices, and the fifth book of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka; teacher of Āśvalāyana. The Śaunaka 'great householder' of the Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad and the Atharvan Śaunaka school's eponym may or may not be the same.

name: Śākalya
summary: Author of the word-by-word text (padapāṭha) of the Ṛgveda, cited by Pāṇini (e.g. 1.1.16) and the Aitareya Āraṇyaka. Some Purāṇic accounts identify him with Vidagdha Śākalya, Yājñavalkya's opponent (tch:vidagdha-sakalya).

name: Śākaṭāyana (the ancient grammarian)
summary: Pre-Pāṇinian grammarian cited by Yāska and Pāṇini (e.g. 3.4.111); author of the thesis that all nouns derive from verbs (Nirukta 1.12). Distinct from the Jain grammarian Pālyakīrti who took his name.

name: Gārgya
summary: Early grammarian cited by Yāska and Pāṇini; held that not all nouns derive from verbs (Nirukta 1.12).

name: Aupamanyava
summary: Early etymologist cited by Yāska, e.g. for 'ṛṣi from seeing: he saw the hymns' (Nirukta 2.11).

name: Vārṣyāyaṇi
summary: Teacher cited by Yāska for the six modifications of being: is born, exists, changes, grows, declines, perishes (Nirukta 1.2).

name: Kautsa
summary: Teacher whose view that Vedic mantras are meaningless is stated and refuted in Nirukta 1.15–16 (known only as reported there).

name: Vyāḍi
summary: Early grammarian, author by tradition of the lost Saṃgraha cited by Patañjali; the Vikṛtivallī on the modified recitations is also ascribed to him (low confidence).

name: Nandikeśvara
summary: Śiva's attendant Nandin, to whom tradition ascribes a verse commentary on the Māheśvara sūtras (and, separately, works on dance); historical authorship uncertain.

name: Jayāditya
summary: Co-author of the Kāśikāvṛtti.

name: Vāmana (co-author of the Kāśikā)
summary: Co-author of the Kāśikāvṛtti; distinct from Vāmana the theorist of poetics.

name: Jinendrabuddhi
summary: Author of the Nyāsa on the Kāśikāvṛtti (a Buddhist, by most accounts).

name: Kaiyaṭa
summary: Kashmiri author of the Pradīpa on the Mahābhāṣya.

name: Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita
summary: Author of the Siddhāntakaumudī and other Pāṇinian works.

name: Varadarāja (grammarian)
summary: Pupil of Bhaṭṭoji Dīkṣita; author of the Laghu- and Madhya-siddhāntakaumudī.

name: Nāgeśa Bhaṭṭa
summary: Last great Pāṇinian of the classical period; his philosophical works belong to lin:vyakarana (U31).

name: Śarvavarman
summary: Author by tradition of the Kātantra grammar, composed for a Sātavāhana king.

name: Candragomin
summary: Buddhist lay scholar, author of the Cāndra grammar (his Buddhist works belong to other units).

name: Pūjyapāda Devanandin
summary: Digambara teacher; U02 adds only his grammar, the Jainendra-vyākaraṇa.

name: Pālyakīrti (Śākaṭāyana)
summary: Yāpanīya Jain grammarian who wrote under the name Śākaṭāyana.

name: Hemacandra
summary: Śvetāmbara polymath; U02 adds only his grammar, the Siddhahemaśabdānuśāsana.

name: Bopadeva
summary: Author of the Mugdhabodha grammar.

name: Durga (Durgācārya)
summary: Commentator on the Nirukta; date uncertain.

name: Skandasvāmin
summary: Commentator on the Ṛgveda and the Nirukta.

name: Devarāja Yajvan
summary: Commentator on the Nighaṇṭu.

name: Halāyudha
summary: Author of the Mṛtasañjīvanī commentary on Piṅgala's Chandaḥśāstra.

name: Sāyaṇa
summary: Author (with collaborators) of commentaries on the Vedic Saṃhitās, Brāhmaṇas and Āraṇyakas; his introductions define the Veda as the text that makes known the non-worldly means to gain the desired and avoid the undesired. Tradition makes him the brother of Mādhava (Vidyāraṇya).

name: Harisvāmin
summary: Commentator on the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (partly surviving).

name: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara
summary: Commentator on the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, Brāhmaṇa and Āraṇyaka (Jñānayajña).

name: Uvaṭa
summary: Commentator on the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā and on the Ṛgveda and Vājasaneyi Prātiśākhyas.

name: Ṣaḍguruśiṣya
summary: Commentator on the Sarvānukramaṇī (Vedārthadīpikā) and the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Sukhapradā).

name: Āpastamba
summary: Founder (sūtrakāra) of the Āpastamba branch of the Taittirīya Black Yajurveda, to whom its whole Kalpasūtra is ascribed.

scholarly.text: c. 3rd c. BCE for the Dharmasūtra (estimates vary)

name: Baudhāyana
summary: Founder (sūtrakāra) of the Baudhāyana branch of the Taittirīya school; its Kalpasūtra is ascribed to him.

scholarly.text: Śrautasūtra among the oldest sūtras (mid-1st millennium BCE); Dharmasūtra core c. 2nd c. BCE

name: Āśvalāyana
summary: Ṛgvedic sūtrakāra, pupil of Śaunaka by tradition, author of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta- and Gṛhyasūtras (he has no surviving Dharma- or Śulbasūtra).

name: Hiraṇyakeśin (Satyāṣāḍha)
summary: Sūtrakāra of the Hiraṇyakeśin branch of the Taittirīya school.

name: Pāraskara
summary: Author by tradition of the White Yajurveda Gṛhyasūtra.

name: Gobhila
summary: Author by tradition of the Kauthuma Sāmaveda Gṛhyasūtra.

name: Lāṭyāyana
summary: Author by tradition of the Kauthuma Sāmaveda Śrautasūtra.

name: Drāhyāyaṇa
summary: Author by tradition of the Rāṇāyanīya Sāmaveda Śrautasūtra.

name: Yājñavalkya
summary: U02 contribution: the authority of ŚB books 1–5 and 11–14, where he answers Janaka on the Agnihotra (11.3.1, 11.6.2), defeats Vidagdha Śākalya on the number of gods (11.6.3) and says he eats beef 'if it is tender' (3.1.2.21); tradition also makes him the lawgiver of the Yājñavalkyasmṛti, which scholars date many centuries later.

tradition.text: the Vedic sage of Janaka's court; the Smṛti presents the same sage teaching in Mithilā

scholarly.text: the Vedic teacher c. 8th–6th c. BCE (if historical); the Yājñavalkyasmṛti c. 3rd–5th c. CE

realization_account.text: He received the White Yajus from the Sun (ŚB 14.9.4.33 = BĀU 6.5.3); in the Purāṇic story he returned the Black Yajus to his teacher Vaiśampāyana by vomiting it.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Śāṇḍilya
summary: The authority of the fire-altar books of the Śatapatha (6–10), whose meditation on the self 'made of mind, with breath for body, of the form of light', smaller than a grain yet greater than the worlds, is the Śāṇḍilya-vidyā (ŚB 10.6.3; ChU 3.14). The Bhakti Sūtra ascribed to a Śāṇḍilya (U25) is a separate, much later attribution.

name: Tura Kāvaṣeya
summary: The first human link in the Agnicayana lineage of ŚB 10.6.5.9, who received it from Prajāpati, who received it from Brahman the self-existent.

name: Aśvapati Kaikeya
summary: King who taught the Vaiśvānara self to brāhmaṇa householders led by Aruṇa Aupaveśi (ŚB 10.6.1; ChU 5.11–18).

name: Mahidāsa Aitareya
summary: The seer to whom the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and Āraṇyaka are ascribed.

realization_account.text: Son of Itarā, slighted by his father, he was favoured by the Earth goddess and received the Brāhmaṇa (Sāyaṇa's introduction); the Chāndogya says he lived 116 years by his knowledge (ChU 3.16.7).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

name: Kauṣītaki
summary: Eponymous teacher of the Kauṣītaki Ṛgveda school.

name: Tittiri
summary: Eponym of the Taittirīya school; the Purāṇas instead derive the name from partridges (tittiri).

name: Vaiśampāyana
summary: Teacher of the Black Yajurveda and, in the Purāṇic story, the teacher with whom Yājñavalkya quarrelled.

name: Jaimini
summary: U02 contribution: eponym of the Jaiminīya Sāmaveda school whose Brāhmaṇa bears his name; tradition makes him the pupil of Vyāsa and the author of the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra (U12).

name: Uddālaka Āruṇi
summary: U02 contribution: in ŚB 11.4.1 he challenges and is defeated by Svaidāyana Śaunaka in a brahmodya; teacher of Yājñavalkya in the vaṃśas.

name: Janaka of Videha
summary: U02 contribution: questions Yājñavalkya and others on the Agnihotra (ŚB 11.3.1; 11.6.2) and is declared a 'brahman' from then on.

name: Vidagdha Śākalya
summary: Yājñavalkya's opponent at Janaka's court, who asks 'how many gods?' and loses his head (ŚB 11.6.3; BĀU 3.9).

name: Videgha Māthava
summary: King who carried Agni Vaiśvānara in his mouth eastward to the Sadānīrā with his priest Gotama Rāhūgaṇa (ŚB 1.4.1.10–17).

name: Śunaḥśepa Ājīgarti
summary: The boy sold by his father Ajīgarta to be sacrificed in place of Rohita, freed by praising the gods, and adopted by Viśvāmitra (AB 7.13–18).

name: Naciketas
summary: U02 contribution: in TB 3.11.8 he is given to Death by his father Vājaśravasa, receives three boons and learns the Nāciketa fire by which he conquers re-death — the Brāhmaṇa root of the Kaṭha Upaniṣad.

name: Bharadvāja
summary: U02 contribution: in TB 3.10.11.3–5 he spends three lives as a Vedic student and is shown by Indra that the Vedas are endless, then taught the Sāvitra fire as 'all knowledge'.

name: Manu Vaivasvata
summary: The present (seventh) Manu, son of Vivasvat; in ŚB 1.8.1 he saves a fish that later tows his ship over the flood, and his offering gives rise to Iḍā.

name: Manu Svāyambhuva
summary: The first Manu, son of the self-existent, who received dharma from Svayambhū and taught it; his teaching is recited in the Manusmṛti by Bhṛgu. Parāśara assigns Manu's dharma to the Kṛta age.

tradition.text: the first Manu, at the beginning of creation

name: Bhṛgu
summary: Seer who recites Manu's teaching in the Manusmṛti (1.59–60), one of Manu's ten mind-born sons (1.35); as Bhṛgu Vāruṇi, son of Varuṇa, he journeys through the other world in ŚB 11.6.1 and JB 1.42–44 (and learns Brahman in TU 3).

name: Gautama (author of the Dharmasūtra)
summary: The Gautama of the Gautama Dharmasūtra, cited by Baudhāyana (BDh 1.1.2.7) and assigned by Parāśara to the Tretā age; distinct from Gautama Akṣapāda of Nyāya.

name: Vasiṣṭha
summary: U02 contribution: the Vedic seer to whom the Vasiṣṭha Dharmasūtra is ascribed.

name: Nārada
summary: U02 contribution: the divine sage to whom the Nāradasmṛti and the Nāradīya Śikṣā are ascribed.

name: Parāśara
summary: U02 contribution: the sage, father of Vyāsa, to whom the Parāśarasmṛti — the code for the Kali age — is ascribed.

name: Bṛhaspati
summary: U02 contribution: the preceptor of the gods, to whom the Bṛhaspatismṛti is ascribed; in the Mahābhāṣya he teaches Indra words one by one. The Lokāyata tradition's Bṛhaspati is treated by U33.

name: Kauṭilya
summary: Author by tradition of the Arthaśāstra.

tradition.text: minister of Candragupta Maurya (late 4th c. BCE)

scholarly.text: author-figure of an Arthaśāstra redacted in the early centuries CE

name: Vātsyāyana Mallanāga
summary: Author of the Kāmasūtra; distinct from Vātsyāyana Pakṣilasvāmin of the Nyāyabhāṣya (tch:vatsyayana).

name: Medhātithi
summary: Author of the oldest surviving commentary on Manu, reasoning in the manner of Mīmāṃsā.

name: Kullūka Bhaṭṭa
summary: Bengali commentator on Manu whose text and numbering became the vulgate.

name: Viśvarūpa
summary: Author of the Bālakrīḍā on Yājñavalkya; tradition identifies him with Sureśvara (tch:suresvara), which scholars doubt.

name: Vijñāneśvara
summary: Author of the Mitākṣarā at the court of Vikramāditya VI of Kalyāṇa.

name: Aparārka (Aparāditya)
summary: Śilāhāra king and commentator on Yājñavalkya.

name: Jīmūtavāhana
summary: Bengali jurist, author of the Dāyabhāga.

name: Lakṣmīdhara
summary: Minister of the Gāhaḍavāla king Govindacandra, author of the Kṛtyakalpataru.

name: Hemādri
summary: Minister of the Yādava kings, author of the Caturvargacintāmaṇi.

name: Raghunandana
summary: Bengali author of the Smṛtitattva.

name: Kamalākara Bhaṭṭa
summary: Author of the Nirṇayasindhu, of the Bhaṭṭa family of Vārāṇasī.

name: Nīlakaṇṭha Bhaṭṭa
summary: Author of the Bhagavantabhāskara (the Mayūkhas).

name: Mitra Miśra
summary: Author of the Vīramitrodaya.

name: Haradatta
summary: Commentator on the Āpastamba and Gautama Dharmasūtras; possibly (uncertain) the author of the Padamañjarī.

name: Maskarin
summary: Commentator on the Gautama Dharmasūtra.

name: Govindasvāmin
summary: Commentator on the Baudhāyana Dharmasūtra.

name: Nandapaṇḍita
summary: Commentator on the Viṣṇusmṛti.

name: Devaṇṇabhaṭṭa
summary: Author of the Smṛticandrikā.

name: Vidyāraṇya (Mādhava)
summary: U02 contribution: tradition identifies the Vijayanagara scholar-minister Mādhava, author of the Parāśaramādhavīya and Kālanirṇaya, with Vidyāraṇya after renunciation; the identification is debated.
